summary: Prove lookup-not-constraint end to end, not just at the inventory store (TKT-235 ai-review)
description:
**Surfaced by TKT-235's ai-review (`gpt-5.6-luna`), finding 5 [medium].** Not a defect that ticket
introduced — a gap between what its tests prove and what its design *claims*.

TKT-235 established the sales-channel registry as a **lookup, not a constraint**: an unregistered —
or disabled — channel code must sell exactly as it did before the registry existed. Two tests guard
it, and both are narrower than the claim:

- `services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go` →
  `TestAnUnregisteredChannelCodeStillSells` calls the **inventory store directly**. It never
  traverses commerce orchestration, catalog fee resolution, split resolution, payments, or any API
  boundary. A registry lookup added at any of those layers would reject the sale *earlier* and leave
  this test green.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/channels_smoke_test.go` → `TestNothingReferencesTheChannelRegistry`
  greps `information_schema` for foreign keys pointing at `channels`. That proves **FK absence in
  catalog's schema**. It says nothing about application-level gating anywhere.

Both had their scope narrowed in comments at review time, so nothing currently overclaims in the
code. What is missing is the test that would actually catch the regression.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A gateway-level (or `smoke/`) test buys through the full path — reserve → fee resolution → split
  resolution → confirm — using a channel code that has **no registry row at all**, and asserts the
  sale completes with the code recorded verbatim on the claim and the order.
- The same path with a channel code whose registry row exists but is **`enabled = false`**, and it
  also completes. Disabling is a *display* decision (it removes the channel from
  `/public/channels`), not a sellability one — nothing in the sale path consults the registry today,
  and this test is what stops that changing silently.
- Both assertions name the invariant and cite ADR-024, so a future ticket that deliberately adds
  registry gating has to change the test and state why, rather than deleting it.

Quality gates: `make check` green. Test-only ticket — if it surfaces a real gating bug in the sale
path, report it and stop rather than fixing it here.

Parent: TKT-17. Non-goals: adding any registry enforcement (that would be the opposite of this
ticket); the seated-pool seam (TKT-176).

governingAdrs.why: The load-bearing decision. The no-FK rule (historical attribution must survive a channel being retired) is what makes 'lookup, not constraint' true. RE-RESOLVED at claim: amended by TKT-246 (allocations may bind a seller via sold_by) and TKT-250 (allocation set carries a revision) since this memo was first captured. Both amendments are guards on channel_allocations, NOT on catalog.channels -- the distinction this test exists to pin.

Fee resolution takes a channel and is one of the layers the end-to-end test must traverse. A registry lookup added here would reject the sale before inventory is ever reached, leaving the inventory-store test green.

Split resolution is channel-selective and is the other such layer. Note it is NOT a separate HTTP call -- splits ride inside the fee-resolution response and are persisted in fee_resolution_snapshot, so traversing fee resolution traverses both.

ADDED at shaping (absent from the 2026-08-09 capture). Per-channel sales windows are the FIRST predicate in the inventory claim guard (window -> seller -> code -> capacity). It gates on channel_allocations, not the registry, but it is a channel-keyed refusal the fixture must not trip, or the test never reaches the INSERT it means to assert on.

governingTests.name: services/commerce/internal/api/channel_seam_test.go
governingTests.why: A LIVE TRIPWIRE, not background. It pins the public reserve route as channel-free until the seam closes, and its header says 'when TKT-246 lands these assertions INVERT; do not delete them' -- then records that they did NOT invert. Any change that makes the public route forward a channel fails here. This ticket must not touch it.

governingTests.name: smoke/coverage_test.go
governingTests.why: Every documented 2xx operation of inventory/commerce/payments/access must be driven by some smoke test, enforced in TestMain. A new smoke file adds coverage, never removes it, but the gate runs on every make check.

governingTests.name: services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:470-497
governingTests.why: The existing test's own scope disclaimer names TKT-241 as the owner of the gateway-level version. Its wording is the charter; the new test should be reachable from it.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Filed from TKT-235 ai-review — incidental, deferred

**Finding:** [medium] *"The lookup-not-constraint regression test does not exercise a sale
boundary"* — `gpt-5.6-luna`, TKT-235 ai-review pass 1.

**Triage: incidental, not blocking.** The reviewer is right that the test is narrower than the
claim, and wrong that this makes the claim false today: nothing in the sale path reads the registry
at all (verified — no reference to `channels` or `ListEnabledChannels` anywhere in commerce or
inventory outside generated types). So there is **no defect in the diff**; there is a missing guard
against a defect a *future* ticket could introduce. Building a full gateway-level purchase harness
is its own vertical slice, well beyond a registry story's scope.

**Done at review time instead:** both tests had their scope narrowed in their own comments, so
neither overclaims in the code. This ticket carries the real coverage.

Needs shaping before Gate 1 — the 8-item DoR is not filled and `first_slice` in particular needs a
decision on whether this rides `smoke/` or the gateway suite.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Shaping pass — 2026-08-16. Verdict: **all 8 items `met`, no open blockers → Gate 1 clears.**

Ran per `references/shaping.md`: read the real code first, then Example-Mapped what was left.
Nothing needed a spike and nothing needs a human decision. Detail is on the `readiness` field;
the four things a reader should not have to diff for:

**1. The COS as filed is partly unachievable, and that is by design — not a bug to fix here.**

The ticket asks for the channel code "recorded verbatim on the claim *and* the order" from a
single full-path purchase. It cannot be, because the **public** route deliberately forwards no
channel to inventory (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:363-381`). TKT-240 added that
forward and it was **reverted** after its own adversarial review — `POST /reservations` is
unauthenticated and takes `channel_code` from the body, so forwarding alone let any caller drain
a reseller's allocation with no credential. TKT-246 then closed the seam only where a channel can
be *authorized* (the partner route, channel from the credential) and kept the public route unable
to reach the decision at all. `channel_seam_test.go:13-58` is a live tripwire pinning exactly
this, with instructions not to delete it.

So `claims.channel_code` is **NULL by design** on a public sale. The ticket text predates TKT-246
and did not know that.

**Correction, not deferral:** the test splits in two, each proving the invariant at the layer that
can actually carry it — **(A) public path** → assert `orders.channel_code` verbatim, having
traversed price + fee (ADR-046) + split (ADR-047) resolution, which are precisely the layers a
registry lookup would be added to; **(B) partner path** → assert `claims.channel_code` *and*
`orders.channel_code` verbatim. Between them the original COS is fully covered, and neither
overclaims. `first_slice` is decided: **`smoke/`**, because there is no separate "gateway suite" —
`smoke/` *is* the gateway-level tier and is already in `make check`.

**2. The invariant is sharper than the ticket words it, and the sharpening is the whole test.**

The claim path guards on **inventory's `channel_allocations`**, never on **catalog's `channels`**.
Two different tables in two different services. The guard is four ordered predicates
(`store.go:500-600`): `window → seller → code → capacity` — and *not one of them* consults the
registry. Writing the test as "a channel with no row sells" without saying *which table* is how it
would end up green and vacuous.

**Guard predicate count, per `shaping.md`:** the fixture must satisfy **all four** to reach the
`INSERT` it asserts on — active allocation for the code, open window, `sold_by` admitting the
caller (or unbound), `requires_code` false, cap ≥ qty. Trip any earlier predicate and the test
proves nothing about the registry while looking like it does. This is the failure mode
`docs/learnings/2026-08-10-a-green-test-that-cannot-reach-the-failing-state.md` names, and the one
the existing inventory test already dodged deliberately (`channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:496`).

**3. The stored context-mémo was stale and has been re-resolved.**

Captured 2026-08-09; since then **ADR-024 took two amendments** (TKT-246 `sold_by`, TKT-250
allocation revision) and **ADR-054** (per-channel sales windows) became the *first* predicate in
the claim guard — and was missing from `governingAdrs` entirely. Added, with the reason it matters
to *this* ticket (it is a channel-keyed refusal the fixture must not trip). All four cited ADRs
verified to resolve at HEAD. `governingTests` added and populated — `channel_seam_test.go` in
particular is a tripwire this ticket must not touch.

**4. Verified, not assumed: nothing on the sale path reads the registry today.**

Zero references to the `channels` table or `ListEnabledChannels` in commerce, inventory, payments
or the gateway; catalog only, plus generated UI types. So there is no gating bug to report — the
ticket's "if it surfaces a real gating bug, stop" branch does not trigger. The `enabled = false`
half is reachable directly at create time (`POST /api/catalog/channels` accepts `enabled`), no
update leg needed.

**`risk:low`: not claimed.** Test-only and touches no production code, which argues for it — but
the work is a *new end-to-end fixture across five services*, and the failure mode being guarded
against is a test that passes without proving anything. That is exactly the class the plan gate
catches. Running the plan gate.

objective.note: TKT-235's 'the channel registry is a lookup, not a constraint' is guarded only by an inventory-store-level test and a catalog FK-absence test. Neither crosses a service boundary, so a registry lookup added in commerce, catalog fee/split resolution, or the gateway would reject a sale earlier and leave both green. This ticket buys the end-to-end guard.

scope.note: IN: new smoke/ test(s) (//go:build smoke, package smoke_test) driving the real docker-compose stack through the gateway. OUT: any registry enforcement (the opposite of this ticket); the seated-pool seam (TKT-176); closing the public-route fee-attribution seam (TKT-247).

uncertainties.note: Resolved by reading at shaping. (1) Nothing on the sale path reads catalog's channels registry: zero hits for ListEnabledChannels / channels-table access in commerce, inventory, payments and gateway; only catalog and generated UI types. (2) The inventory claim guard reads channel_allocations (inventory's OWN table), never catalog.channels -- the two are distinct and conflating them is the trap this test must not fall into. (3) No allowlist gating: scripts/smoke.sh:304 runs go test -tags smoke ./... with no -run, so a new file cannot silently never run.

dependencies.note: No blocked-by links, none needed. Depends only on infrastructure that already exists: scripts/smoke.sh's stack lifecycle, the SMOKE_PARTNER_TOKEN/CHANNEL/RESELLER_ID credentials it enrols (smoke.sh:260-274), and the publishedSlot / internalJSON / partnerDo / created helpers.

approach.note: VERIFIED AGAINST THE CODE, and it corrects the ticket text. The ticket's COS asks for the code 'recorded verbatim on the claim AND the order' from one path. That is not achievable from one path, and the reason is deliberate: the PUBLIC route POST /api/commerce/reservations forwards no channel to inventory at all (services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:363-381; TKT-240 forwarded it and was REVERTED because that route is unauthenticated; TKT-246 kept it closed). channel_seam_test.go:13-58 is a live tripwire pinning that. So claims.channel_code is NULL by design on a public sale. The test therefore splits in two, each proving the invariant at the layer that can carry it: (A) PUBLIC path -- unregistered channel_code in the body, reserve -> price/fee/split resolution -> order confirm; assert 2xx and orders.channel_code == the code verbatim. This traverses ADR-046 fee resolution and ADR-047 split resolution, the exact layers a registry lookup would be added to. (B) PARTNER path -- POST /api/commerce/partners/reservations under SMOKE_PARTNER_TOKEN, whose channel comes from the CREDENTIAL, then confirm via POST /api/commerce/orders; assert claims.channel_code AND orders.channel_code == the code. 'reseller-smoke' already has no catalog registry row (smoke.sh never creates one), which is the unregistered case for free. Template: smoke/partner_reserve_test.go:27-107 plus a confirm leg. GUARD PREDICATE COUNT on the claim path (services/inventory/internal/store/store.go:500-600): the ordered sequence is window -> seller -> code -> capacity, four predicates, ALL of them keyed on channel_allocations and NONE on catalog.channels. The test must reach the INSERT, so its fixture must satisfy all four -- an active allocation for the code, open window, sold_by admitting the caller (or unbound), requires_code false, cap >= qty. A fixture that fails any earlier predicate proves nothing about the registry, which is precisely how this test could be green and vacuous.

first_slice.note: DECIDED: smoke/, not the gateway suite -- there is no separate 'gateway suite'. smoke/ IS the gateway-level tier (module ticketing/smoke, black-box HTTP against the running compose stack via SMOKE_GATEWAY_URL), and it is already in make check (Makefile:20 -> :122). One new file, both halves (A and B) plus the enabled=false variant, fits one slice.

success.note: COS restated to what the code permits -- see the readiness comment. Three assertions: unregistered code sells on the public path (order verbatim); unregistered code sells on the partner path (claim AND order verbatim); a registry row with enabled=false sells identically on both. Each names the invariant in its comment and cites ADR-024.

context_memo.note: Baked and RE-RESOLVED at shaping. The stored memo was captured 2026-08-09 and is stale: ADR-024 has since taken two amendments (TKT-246 sold_by, TKT-250 revision), and ADR-054 (per-channel sales windows) became a claim-path guard after capture and was absent from the list. Corrected below; all cited ADRs verified to resolve at HEAD under docs/adr/.
